label: b45: continue the 4 best b29/b40 checkpoints to 5M, lr 1e-8
notes:
Continues b29b-chase10g75seed2 from its own best checkpoint, ckpt-1447000 (99.0% over 500 episodes, rank 1 of 8 and the project record), to an absolute 5M-step cap with SNEK_LEARNING_RATE=1e-8. Seed matches the source arm.

Fourth rung of the learning-rate ladder on the same four seeded champions: b42 = 1e-5 (the rate these checkpoints were trained at), b43 = 1e-6, b44 = 1e-7, b45 = 1e-8. Seeds, config and source checkpoints are identical across all four, so the batches are a paired dose-response on one knob. Config is b29's: fc320, chase-safe c=0.10 gate 75, IS off, target_update 1000, discount 0.9975, food-distance 0, fork_branches 4, and NO free-space shaping.

WHY THIS RUNG. The ladder is monotone and decelerating. Over the +1487k window common to b43 and b44, per-seed differences were +4.6 / +1.0 / +1.6 / +0.8 -- 4 of 4 for the lower rate, mean +2.0 pp, against +4.9 pp for the 1e-5 -> 1e-6 step. Nothing yet separates 'plateau' from 'slope', and this rung is the measurement that does. b42's HOF-500 gives the other end of the scale: at 1e-5 the only checkpoints surviving a flat 500 episodes at >=98% sit within 75k steps of the seed, and b42a's best (98.4% at 1453k) is BELOW b29b's own 99.0% starting figure -- so 1e-5 keeps nothing it earns.

WHY THE CAP IS 5M AND NOT 3M -- the one deliberate difference from b42/b43/b44. The peak arrives later at every rung: b42's best_perfect30 peaked AT its seed step, b43's at 1527k-2803k, b44's at 1814k / 2190k / 2230k / 2460k, i.e. 300-1100k steps past seed. If that timescale keeps stretching with the rate, a 3M cap would stop these arms BEFORE their peak and the batch would report a null that is really truncation -- which is exactly the 'it will just freeze' reading that was already wrong once, at 1e-7. 5M gives each arm ~3.5-3.65M steps past seed against b44's ~1.49-1.65M. This introduces no confound: the cap cannot change the trajectory, only where it stops, so every cross-rung comparison is still made over the matched +1487k window and is unaffected. The extra steps are strictly additional information. Expect roughly 20 h of wall clock for the wave.

PRE-REGISTERED READINGS, written before launch. Note the previous rung's pre-registration was WRONG -- it put ~65% on a null and the ~25% 'lower is better' branch won -- so these are stated with that in mind.
(1) b45 BEATS b44 by a further small margin, ~+0.5 to +1.5 pp, 3-4 of 4 seeds -- ~45%. The ladder is a slope, not a plateau, and the useful rate is lower still. Would justify a 1e-9 rung, though at some point the step size stops mattering because it is below the scale at which the weights affect the argmax.
(2) NULL against b44, inside +/-0.5 pp -- ~40%. The plateau is real and sits between 1e-7 and 1e-8. This is the outcome that closes the ladder, and it is the one to plan around: it means 1e-7 is the operating point.
(3) b45 is WORSE than b44 -- ~15%. Two distinguishable mechanisms, and the peak's timing tells them apart. If b45 is worse AND still climbing at the 5M cap, it is too slow rather than wrong -- truncation, and the cap should go up again. If b45 is worse and FLAT from early on, the step size has fallen below the scale that changes the greedy action and the arm is genuinely frozen; that is the real failure mode this ladder has been looking for, and it would put a floor under the useful rate.
READ THE PEAK'S TIMING, NOT ONLY ITS HEIGHT. best_perfect30's step is the discriminator between 'frozen' and 'still improving', and it is what made b44's result legible.

DO NOT USE peak_trailing TO JUDGE THESE ARMS. It is trailing average SCORE, which maxes at 95/95, and every arm in b42/b43/b44 read exactly 95.0 with the peak timestamped at its seed step -- the metric is saturated from the first eval because these policies already play a full board. Read perfect_percent, best_perfect30 or strong_eval_fraction instead.

BUDGET THE CLOSE-OUT AT 8-15 HOURS. top20's N is a target, not a quota: every checkpoint whose 10-episode graph eval reached >=90% is measured past N. A continuation arm sits above that threshold for its whole run, so b43's four arms selected 791 / 1196 / 803 / 826 checkpoints rather than 20. With a 5M cap b45 will select more still. A close-out running many hours is expected here, not hung.

TRIPWIRE. Adam's learning_rate is a checkpointed tf.Variable, so initialize_or_restore() puts the saved 1e-5 back and SNEK_LEARNING_RATE was a silent no-op on every resume before training.enforce_learning_rate (2026-08-18). Each arm MUST print
  learning rate: checkpoint restored 1e-05, reset to the configured 1e-08
at startup. If that line is absent the arm is training at 1e-5, it is a second copy of b42, and the batch measures nothing -- check it before reading any result.

SEEDING. Pre-seeded by hyperparamTuning/scripts/seed_from_checkpoint.sh: arch.json, one ckpt pair, a copy of the source arm's replay_buffer, and a 'checkpoint' state file naming only that step. initialize_or_restore() would otherwise take the source's LAST step rather than its best; resuming in place would overwrite the arm the selection was made from; and one pre-existing checkpoint guarantees every later ckpt-* belongs to this run, so the close-out cannot mix two arms' weights at the same step. The buffer is carried deliberately -- without it a 5k-step test of a 98% policy fell 80% -> 50% perfect, and held 90-100% with it.
